system.name: SPEX
system.one_liner: a speculative exploration framework that breaks the reward-feedback barrier in tree-of-thought reasoning

content.subject: how speculative exploration removes the reward-feedback wait that blocks BFS and DFS search-tree expansion

panels.label: (a) reward barrier
panels.differs: template: both BFS and DFS stall at a dashed 'wait' point until reward-model feedback for all pending branches arrives

content.key_idea: Both breadth-first and depth-first tree-of-thought search must pause at a synchronization point to wait for reward-model feedback before continuing; SPEX's speculative exploration instead keeps expanding speculative branches through that point without waiting.
content.reading_order: Top-down through Breadth-First then Depth-First Search in panel (a), each ending at a dashed wait point, then the same order in panel (b) where speculative boxes replace the wait.

style.fill: flat pastel fills (blue-grey, peach, green) for the three box kinds
style.stroke: thin dark-navy outlines (#192d54) on every box and arrow, dashed for not-yet-reached placeholder boxes and the wait marker
style.arrows: thin dashed and solid navy arrows connect boxes along each branch, with angled back-propagation arrows feeding a reward back to an earlier node

encoding.color_means: grey-blue marks plain reasoning-output boxes, peach marks reward-score boxes, and green (added only in panel b) marks speculative reasoning-output boxes
encoding.line_style_means: dashed lines and boxes mark branches not yet expanded or the wait synchronization point; solid lines connect already-produced steps; angled arrows show back-propagation of a reward to an earlier node
encoding.state_means: panel (a) freezes at a dashed 'wait' point before reward feedback returns; panel (b) instead continues past that point with green speculative boxes and dashed not-yet-resolved placeholders
encoding.marker_means: no numbered markers; the printed numbers (0.9, 0.8, 0.5, length values) are the reward and length values themselves, not step indices
encoding.emphasis: the added green speculative-output boxes in panel (b), replacing the grey dashed wait gap of panel (a), visually carry the contribution
reusable_patterns: identical BFS and DFS branch templates redrawn in a before/after pair, with new coloured boxes filling in what used to be a blocking wait
weaknesses: the same reward value 0.5 labels two different BFS branches, so it is not clear whether they are coincidentally equal or a simplification
the DFS 'Back Propagation' arrows are not numbered, so the order of propagation among the three shown rewards (0.9, 0.8, 0.5) is not fully explicit

evidence: the system must pause to await feedback from the reward model before determining the next action
faster branches are forced to idle until the global aggregation completes
SPEX proactively and speculatively explores promising candidate branches based on predictive signals

summary: Figure 3 contrasts the reward barrier that stalls tree-of-thought search with SPEX's speculative fix, using the same Breadth-First and Depth-First Search templates in both panels. In (a), BFS fans out into parallel branches (labelled with token counts like 150, Length: 400, 200) each scored by a reward box (0.9, 0.5), but must wait at a dashed synchronization point until every branch's reward returns before picking the next expansion budget; DFS similarly advances one path with back-propagated rewards (0.9, 0.8, 0.5) but must wait for feedback before deciding whether to continue or backtrack. In (b), green Speculative Reasoning Output boxes and dashed placeholder branches fill in exactly where the wait used to block progress, so both BFS and DFS keep expanding predicted branches while the true reward is still pending.
summary_zh: 图3对比奖励壁垒与SPEX的推测式解决方案：(a)中BFS并行分支和DFS单路径都需在虚线等待点等待奖励模型反馈才能继续；(b)中绿色推测推理输出和虚线占位分支填补等待处，使搜索无需等待即可继续扩展。
